section: Educational Psychology · Ch2 — Piaget: Cognitive Development
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A toddler who has only ever seen small dogs sees a large horse for the first time and confidently calls it 'big dog', fitting the new animal into her existing 'dog' schema without changing that schema at all. In Piaget's terms, this is:
explanation: Assimilation incorporates new information into an EXISTING schema without altering it (the horse is squeezed into the 'dog' category as-is) — accommodation, by contrast, would involve MODIFYING or creating a new schema (e.g., forming a separate 'horse' category) once the mismatch becomes clear.
